notes: Direct HTTP fetch of www.otto.de worked with zero blocking (Tier 1, no proxy/curl_cffi needed, consistent with the prior Home-Decor pass for this company). robots.txt already checked and cleared in the prior Home-Decor pass (no Claude-specific disallow on category paths). OTTO's pet department lives at /tierbedarf/ (site nav labels it 'Tierbedarf' = pet supplies), reached from the homepage mega-menu, with 9 second-level animal-type hubs: Hunde (Dogs), Katzen (Cats), Pferde (Horses), Aquaristik (Fish/Aquatics), Vögel (Birds/Poultry), Kleintiere (Small Animals), Wildtiere (Wild Animals), Tierfutter (Pet Food index), Terraristik (Reptiles). Each animal hub (except Pferde, which has no clean hub path and is generated as a bundled /?selektion=... filtered listing instead) exposes the same client-rendered local-navigation widget used successfully in the prior pass (li.nav_local-link data-title=... span.nav_link-count data-count=N), generated from the live search index; some children link via a plain href, others via an obfuscated base64 'data-ub64e' attribute that decodes to a '/?selektion=(...)' filter query — both are genuine crawlable PLP URLs and were decoded/kept. QTY VERIFICATION: spot-checked 5 leaves by directly fetching their PLP and reading the rendered 'N Produkte' header (span.reptile-item-count__item-count / data-item-count) against the nav data-count snapshot: Hundetransport (nav 5101 vs rendered 5099), Kratzmöbel (nav 3376 vs rendered 3375), Pferde bundle (nav 3754 vs rendered 3758), Terrarien (597 vs 597, exact), Aquarien (944 vs 944, exact) — all within 0-4 of each other, i.e. normal live-inventory drift between separate fetches seconds apart, not a data-source error; used the freshly-rendered value for those 5 leaves and the nav snapshot (with evidence) for the rest. EXCLUSIONS: Wildtiere (wild animals/insects/hedgehogs/sparrows/bees with insect-hotel and wildlife-house products, decoded selektion query confirms tierart=bienen/eichelhaeher/igel/insekten/spatzen/wespen/wildtiere/wildvoegel etc.) was excluded entirely as non-pet wildlife/garden products, not pet ownership. Within the Kleintiere (Small Animals) hub, dropped 'Insektenhotels' (its href resolves to /garten/gartendekoration/insektenhotels/ - a Garden Decoration product, cross-listed into the small-animal facet, not a genuine small-pet product) and 'Pferdeputzzeug' (Horse Grooming Kit, mislabelled into the Kleintiere facet — already covered by the Horses group) per the do-not-steal-from-other-categories / no-cross-species-mislabelling rule. DEDUP: the standalone 'Tierfutter' (/tierbedarf/futter/) hub is an index of the exact same per-species food URLs already captured under each animal's own section (Hundefutter/Katzenfutter/Fischfutter/Vogelfutter/Kleintiere-Futter share identical URL+count with their animal-hub counterpart) — not re-emitted as duplicate rows, per the same-URL/same-listing overlap rule; only its Pferde (Horse Food, 125) child was net-new and added under Horses, since the bundled horse selektion listing does not expose food as its own page. All food/feed leaves flagged MANUAL REVIEW: PET CONSUMABLE per the open policy gap (no include/exclude decision made). No medical/veterinary categories were found in the pet taxonomy. Hühnerställe/Hühnertränken (chicken coops/waterers) were kept — OTTO places them inside the Vögel (Birds) pet-supplies branch itself, not a separate livestock/agriculture department, so treated as in-scope backyard-poultry pet care per the site's own taxonomy; flagged nowhere further since no livestock-vs-pet policy exists in the brief. Absence check: browsed the homepage mega-menu (found /tierbedarf/ directly), the /tierbedarf/ hub's own local-nav (9 animal-type children), and each animal hub's own local-nav (2nd-level children) — no site search substitution used, real navigation was sufficient and decisive.
